Categories.value: Featured pictures of architecture in Germany|Self-published work|Featured pictures by Aristeas|Photographs by Aristeas - by name|Information field template with formatting|Featured pictures of Baden-Württemberg|Featured abstract photos|Featured minimalist photos|Abstract photography in Germany|Photographs by Aristeas - by ID|Quality abstract photos|Decorative glass|2021 in Bad Rappenau|Baden-Württemberg photographs taken on 2021-07-21|Photographs taken by Aristeas in 2021|SRGB images|Windows in Bad Rappenau|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation (49° N, 9° E)|Photographs of Bad Rappenau by Aristeas|Taken with Sony ILCE-7RM4 and Sony FE 90mm F2.8 Macro G OSS

ImageDescription.value: The photo shows a detail of a window, ca. 8.5 × 5.7 cm (3.35 × 2.23 inch). The window pane is made from a simple kind of so-called decorative glass (a.k.a. patterned glass, textured or obscure glass), produced about 2013; the vertical stripes in the photo are produced by the fluted structure of the glass. The decorative glass acts as a diffuser. The colours you see in the photo are actually an image of the outside world, but heavily diffused or “abstracted” by the decorative glass; the red comes from the roof of a house, the green from the plants in the garden. Because the glass works as a diffuser, everything in the photo consists of smaller and larger gradations. IMHO it’s amazing that something as simple as a fluted window pane, if you only look closely enough, shows these complex gradients and creates an abstract image.

ImageDescription.value:
Photo art based on a photo of the Viktorkirmes (Ferris wheel “Columbia Rad” on Münsterstraße, corner Coesfelder Straße) in Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
The original shot used the creative technique of intentional camera movement. This image was mirrored and recomposed several times to achieve the symmetry effect.
Two traditional folk festivals are particularly important in Dülmen: the Trinity Fair and the Victor Fair.
The Trinity Fair takes place around the church festival of the Holy Trinity in early summer. Its origins lie in religious celebrations and processions, which over time developed into a secular folk festival. With market stalls, fairground rides, and music, it became an integral part of urban life.
The Viktorkirmes in autumn is associated with the patron saint of the city, Saint Victor. It also has ecclesiastical roots and dates back to earlier church consecration and patron saint festivals. In the 19th and 20th centuries, both fairs grew into important annual markets.
Today, modern rides, traditional stalls, and a colorful supporting program characterize both festivals. They combine religious tradition, customs, and communal celebration and are an integral part of Dülmen’s identity.

Artist.value: Dietmar Rabich
